findings.title: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants manage access when caller only has VIEW permission
findings.body: In `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()`, the permission check calls `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. Because `AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW` is included in the expected scopes, an admin who only has the `view` scope on all groups will have `canManage()` evaluate to `true`. Since `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` guards group creation and moving existing groups to the top level with `auth.groups().requireManage()`, a read-only admin with `view` permission on groups can create new top-level groups or move existing groups to the top level. `canManage()` should only check `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` (and the Javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` at line 75 should be updated accordingly).

findings.title: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() never resolves group IDs and returns resource UUIDs instead
findings.body:
`GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is broken in three ways:

1. `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource()` never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)` when creating a resource for an individual group; only the all-groups resource (`"Groups"`) created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` has its type set to `AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE`. As a result, `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` never visits any individual group resources, returning an empty set for per-group permissions. This causes `UsersResource.getUsersCount()` to return `0` and `UsersResource.getUsers()` / `BruteForceUsersResource.searchUser()` to not set `UserModel.GROUPS` on the session (breaking paginated user queries for group admins).
2. Inside the `findByType` consumer, `groupResource.getId()` is passed to `hasPermission(...)` and added to `granted`. However, `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource()` stores the `GroupModel` ID in `groupResource.getName()`, while `groupResource.getId()` is the internal authorization `Resource` UUID. Because `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` looks up resources via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`, passing `groupResource.getId()` misses the group resource (falling back to the all-groups resource), and `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` puts the authorization `Resource` UUID into `UserModel.GROUPS` instead of the `GroupModel` ID.
3. Because the all-groups resource (`name = "Groups"`) has `type = "Groups"`, `findByType` visits it. If an admin has `view-members` or `manage-members` on all groups, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` adds the all-groups resource's UUID to `granted`, causing `UsersResource` and `BruteForceUsersResource` to filter user queries by a non-existent group ID and return no users.

findings.title: Javadoc for requireManageMembers references canManageMembership instead of canManageMembers
findings.body: The Javadoc for `requireManageMembers(GroupModel group)` states `Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns {@code false}.` It should reference `{@link #canManageMembers(GroupModel)}`.
